sourceEvidence.label: PERSONA LIFF member platform source and contract tests

assessment.summary: Source evidence supports centralizing action contracts and decomposing frontend and GAS composition roots while preserving the existing dual-GAS authorization boundary.

nonNegotiables: Preserve separate member and administrator LINE audiences and GAS deployments.
Preserve request-id idempotency and fetch-first bridge-fallback behavior.
Do not migrate or delete persistent data without separate authorization.
Do not deploy external services as part of this design phase.
assumptions: No measured production traffic, latency, memory, lock-contention, or row-count budget was supplied.
Existing public request and response contracts must remain backward compatible during migration.
The current Google Sheets datastore remains adequate unless measurements show otherwise.

opportunities.title: Centralize action contracts while preserving dual-GAS isolation
opportunities.summary: Move payload ownership out of the shared transport, decompose page composition roots, and bind each backend action to one deployment-owned validator, policy, handler, and response contract.
opportunities.diagnosis: Action names and fields are manually synchronized across browser controllers, one shared transport whitelist, GAS parsers, validators, dispatch chains, and tests; the server currently fails closed, but ownership dispersion raises compatibility and future control-drift risk.

evidence.claim: The repository architecture document identifies member and admin front-controller coupling, transport/domain-field coupling, and single-file GAS deployments.
The shared transport owns a cross-domain EXTRA_FIELD_NAMES whitelist used by both fetch and bridge serialization.
The member front controller owns LIFF session, profile, point claims, scanner, history, UI, and request composition state.
Three administrator pages share one state container and branch their boot and interaction behavior through ADMIN_PAGE.
The member deployment repeats action ownership across a fail-fast allowlist, conditional dispatch, parsing, and action-specific validation.
The administrator deployment repeats action ownership across ADMIN_ACTIONS, conditional dispatch, parsing, and action-specific validation.
Because action-field ownership spans multiple manually synchronized layers, future changes have a larger compatibility and preventive-control drift surface than a deployment-owned command registry.

desiredInvariants: Each deployment rejects unknown actions before configuration, LINE verification, or Spreadsheet access.
Each action binds input normalization, authorization policy, handler, idempotency policy, and response projection at one deployment-owned registry entry.
The shared browser transport understands only the request envelope and an already validated payload.
Member and administrator LINE audiences and privileged handlers remain isolated by deployment.
Mutating retries preserve the same request ID until a definitive outcome is known.
Spreadsheet schema, locks, reads, writes, and uniqueness checks are owned by repository modules.

options.title: Targeted extraction and stronger contract tests
options.summary: Extract only high-change controllers and validators while retaining the shared field whitelist and conditional GAS dispatch.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Local extractions reduce selected coupling but do not change overall ownership.
The transport retains the shared domain field whitelist.
Only selected member use cases leave the front controller.
Page branches remain but can gain local helpers.
Tests cover manual member action synchronization without consolidating it.
Tests cover manual admin action synchronization without consolidating it.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional action-matrix tests detect drift earlier, but field and dispatch ownership remains dispersed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Mutate each action inventory in a test fixture and require a deterministic contract mismatch failure.

tradeoffs.assessment: No network hop or datastore behavior changes; page initialization may improve only where code is conditionally extracted.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare transferred bytes, parse time, boot time, and request counts on the same demo pages.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small controller objects replace equivalent shared state without adding a runtime service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare browser heap snapshots after member and each admin page reaches idle.

tradeoffs.assessment: Selected state machines are isolated, while global lifecycle and manual contract drift remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run retry, cancellation, navigation, and stale-request regression tests for each extracted controller.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deployment topology and health checks do not change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify existing deployment instructions and health responses remain valid.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small facade-preserving changes are easy to stage and revert.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require each extraction to pass the full suite before removing its legacy code path.

residualRisks: Manual GAS action lists, validators, and dispatch can drift.

workPackages: Extract one high-change controller at a time behind the current facade.
acceptanceCriteria: Public actions and responses remain unchanged.
Each extraction has state and retry regression coverage.
migrationNotes: Do not remove the legacy facade until the new controller is active on all entry pages.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the individual controller script and restore its legacy script tag or function block.

options.title: Modular dual-GAS applications
options.summary: Use page composition roots and action adapters in the browser, envelope-only transport, and a command registry plus repository modules in each independent GAS deployment.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Implements the documented modular dependency direction while retaining dual deployment.
Moves domain fields from transport to action adapters.
Replaces the member front controller with bounded composition roots and use cases.
Gives each admin page its own state and controller composition.
Binds member validators, policies, handlers, and responses in one registry while preserving fail-fast rejection.
Binds admin validators, authorization, handlers, and responses in one registry while preserving fail-fast rejection.

tradeoffs.assessment: Contract and control ownership becomes reviewable at each deployment boundary without merging member and admin authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Enumerate both registries and prove unknown and cross-role actions fail before config, LINE, or Sheets.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new network hop is introduced, and page-specific roots can avoid unrelated initialization; actual browser savings are unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare transferred bytes, parse/evaluate time, boot duration, and backend requests for all demo entry pages.

tradeoffs.assessment: Registries and injected services add bounded objects while page roots can remove unrelated shared state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare idle heap and retained DOM listeners per page before and after migration.

tradeoffs.assessment: State, handler, repository, and retry responsibilities gain explicit owners and failure boundaries.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run lifecycle, idempotency, bridge/fetch parity, stale-response, and lock-contention tests per action.

tradeoffs.assessment: Multi-file GAS source requires a reproducible deployment checklist or tooling to prevent partial copies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Perform a dry-run build/deploy manifest check and verify both health versions before frontend cutover.

tradeoffs.assessment: Compatibility facades and ordered dual-GAS rollout are required, though no data schema migration is needed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Stage one page and one read-only action first, rehearse rollback, then migrate mutations.

residualRisks: Google Sheets still requires locks, rereads, and uniqueness checks for cross-row mutations.
Browser contracts remain untrusted and cannot replace GAS validation.
Manual Apps Script publishing can still produce source/deployment drift.

workPackages: Freeze action inventory and compatibility facades.
Introduce action adapters and envelope-only transport.
Split admin and member composition roots.
Introduce command registries and repository modules in each GAS deployment.
Measure page boot and Sheet lock behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Public request and response behavior remains backward compatible.
Unknown and cross-role actions fail before privileged work.
No persistent schema or data changes occur.
All relevant tests pass and both deployed health versions are explicitly verified after authorized deployment.
migrationNotes: Keep the legacy transport field adapter until every action adapter is active.
Deploy administrator GAS, then member GAS, then frontend, with health/version checks between stages.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the previous frontend script tags or facade and select the prior immutable deployment version for each GAS; no data rollback is required because the schema is unchanged.

options.title: Managed APIs with a transactional ledger
options.summary: Replace core GAS and Sheets transaction paths with separate managed member/admin policy services and a transactional datastore.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Replaces large runtime boundaries but must preserve separate member/admin authority.
Managed API contracts replace the shared transport field whitelist.
A new client adapter boundary still requires decomposed member state.
A new client adapter boundary still requires page-specific admin roots.
The member command surface moves to a managed policy service.
The admin command surface moves to a separately authorized managed policy service.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service identities, transactional constraints, and telemetry can strengthen controls, but new secrets, network, database, and operational surfaces appear.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model the selected platform, verify separate service identities and least-privilege database roles, and perform a scoped security review before cutover.

tradeoffs.assessment: Indexed transactional queries may outperform Sheet scans, while service cold starts and an additional platform can add latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark production-like row counts and concurrency for login, redemption, draw, and admin list p50/p95/p99 latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: Service runtimes, database connections, buffers, and telemetry add resources beyond static pages and GAS execution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure runtime memory, connection counts, and per-request allocation under representative load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Transactions improve mutation atomicity, but service, database, migration, and networking failure modes increase.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run failover, retry, duplicate command, partial migration, and dependency outage tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Monitoring, backups, patching, secrets rotation, incident response, and cost controls become required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete an operational readiness review with ownership, alerts, backup restore, retention, and cost budgets.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing Sheets data and two deployed contracts require dual-write or freeze/backfill/reconcile/cutover/rollback planning.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reconcile every entity and ledger total in a staging migration and rehearse rollback with the GAS compatibility path retained.

residualRisks: Incorrectly merging member and admin policy services would increase blast radius.
Data migration and dual-write reconciliation can corrupt reward balances if not exact.
New platform secrets and telemetry create additional sensitive-data obligations.

workPackages: Design separate service identities and transactional schema.
Build migration reconciliation and compatibility paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Measured capacity or consistency requirements justify migration.
Backup restore and rollback are rehearsed.
migrationNotes: Do not remove GAS until post-cutover reconciliation and rollback windows close.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Route LIFF clients back to the GAS compatibility endpoints and replay only reconciled commands; keep a defined reverse-sync path until the migration window closes.

opportunities.recommendation: Choose modular dual-GAS applications under the current balanced compatibility constraints; choose targeted extraction for a much smaller change budget, or managed APIs only after measured Sheets and concurrency limits justify the migration.

openQuestions: May a later implementation introduce a reproducible multi-file Apps Script deployment workflow such as clasp?
What are the production Sheet row counts, peak concurrent mutations, p95 login latency, and lock timeout rates?
Should the pre-existing lottery-center-button CSS contract failure be fixed separately before architecture implementation?
